title: Widows and the poor
hookLine: the one who runs errands for widows and the poor is like one striving in the path of Allah
tomorrow: what do the Torah and the Qur'an both say about strangers?

lines: A BIG PHRASE FOR A SMALL FAVOR.
cards: A grandmother asks you to call someone every Sunday. It sounds like the smallest favor in the world: fifteen minutes, a question about her knee, the same story about her late husband, again. Nobody posts about it.
Nobody claps. Can something that small count as a struggle? In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reaches for a surprisingly big phrase for exactly this kind of help.

teach.h: LIKE ONE STRIVING IN ALLAH'S PATH.
teach.b: Here's the hadith: the one who works for the widow and the poor is like one who strives in the path of Allah. In another version: like one who prays all night and fasts all day.

teach.h: A HEAVY PHRASE, PINNED TO ERRANDS.
teach.b: The path of Allah is a heavy phrase. In the Qur'an it goes with costly things: giving your wealth, leaving your home, risking your life. And here it's pinned to errands.
Groceries carried up the stairs. A form filled out at the kitchen table. A ride to the clinic.

teach.h: SA'I: BACK AND FORTH, EVERY WEEK.
teach.b: The hadith's word for the helper is sa'i: the one who keeps going back and forth. Not one heroic act. Legwork, repeated.
Why would errands stand next to a night of prayer? One reading: because the need doesn't stop. A widow's needs don't trend.
They come back every week, quietly, and the person who keeps meeting them is doing something steady that nobody films. The Qur'an names the same people among those who are owed.
In 2:177, righteousness isn't only facing east or west in prayer; it includes giving wealth, for love of Him, to relatives, orphans, the needy and the traveler.
Care for the widow and the poor isn't a side project next to faith. In the hadith, it's the same road.

how: Muslims look after widows and the poor through zakat and sadaqah, mosque food and visiting programs, and family duty; many point to this hadith to say steady, everyday help is worship.

games.q: what does “widows and the poor” mean?
o: people whose quiet needs come back each week
people who gave everything away for God
women who never married and live alone

games.q: what's inside the hadith — tap the pairs.
p: the one who keeps going back and forth
a heavy phrase, pinned to errands
like praying all night, fasting all day
giving to relatives, orphans, the needy

s: 'in the path of Allah' in this hadith is about fighting
the hadith gives that honor to the one who works for widows and the poor.
one version compares this help to praying all night and fasting all day
that's the second wording in Sahih al-Bukhari.
the hadith praises one big gift over steady help
its word is sa'i: the one who keeps going back and forth.

games.q: a widower down your street keeps missing trash day since his wife died, and the bins are piling up. you're busy. what does today's hadith point to?
o: roll his bins out each week, and knock to say hi while you're there.
tape the city's trash schedule to his door so he can keep track.
leave it; helping might make him feel like he can't cope alone.
games.why: the hadith's sa'i is the one who keeps going back. the weekly errand is the striving, like the path of Allah.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose week runs thin: a widowed neighbor, a grandparent, an auntie who lives alone. Write the first line of a message to them, just the first line, and decide which day you'll send it.

wordCard.voice: Widows and the poor: people whose needs are quiet and come back every week. In the hadith, the one who keeps meeting them is like one striving in the path of Allah.

orig.note: Arabic: the one who strives, who goes back and forth on someone's behalf; the hadith's word for the helper.

carryVoice: Carry this: like the path of Allah, only it runs past a neighbor's door. See you soon.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5353 (also 6006, 6007; Sahih Muslim 2982): the one who works for the widow and the poor is like the one who strives in the path of Allah, or like one who prays all night and fasts all day
Qur'an 2:177 (righteousness is not turning to east or west, but includes giving wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer)
